narrative:
The model estimates you have a 31% chance of failing your final year. This is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses to strengthen your preparation.

The prediction is driven mainly by three aspects of your situation. The most influential factor is that you have had no past class failures. While this is the same as the average for students who passed, in your specific combination of circumstances the model sees it as insufficient to offset other risks. Second, although you clearly want to pursue higher education, this strong ambition is not yet backed by the study habits needed to turn that goal into reality. Third, your mother works in the services sector, which the model associates with a slightly elevated chance of struggling compared with students whose mothers are teachers or in health-related roles.

Taken together, these elements tipped the model toward expecting you might not pass. Your very low weekly study time, long travel distance to school, and high weekend social activity further reinforce this outlook, even though you have strong family relationships, no romantic distractions, and zero absences so far.

To improve, focus immediately on building a realistic study routine of at least two hours most days. Use your clear desire for higher education as motivation to turn that ambition into consistent daily effort. Speak with your teachers about targeted support; small, steady changes in how you spend your after-school time can meaningfully raise your chances of success.
